PART 1 - header hygiene, applies to every file under include/.
- No header may include another header of this project: when you are done, no file under include/ contains an `#include "..."` line. Angle-bracket standard library includes are fine, and each header must include the ones it needs.
- The word `inline` must not appear anywhere under include/.
- Every header must compile on its own: `echo '#include "door.hpp"' | g++ -std=c++20 -Iinclude -fsyntax-only -x c++ -` must succeed for each header, and likewise for the other four.
- A member function that needs another class of this project moves out of line into src/<same stem>.cpp. Create src/room.cpp (holding Room::neighbours), src/door.cpp (holding Door::label) and src/keyring.cpp (holding Keyring::collectFrom), plus anything else that has to move with them. src/campus.cpp already exists.
- Delete include/campus_all.hpp. Nothing may include it.
- Public signatures and observable behaviour stay exactly as they are. Do NOT modify src/main.cpp.

PART 2 - Ledger<T> must stop being a header-only template.
- include/ledger.hpp keeps the class with member DECLARATIONS only, and ends the namespace with explicit instantiation declarations for exactly the two element types this project uses: `extern template class Ledger<int>;` and `extern template class Ledger<std::string>;`.
- Create src/ledger.cpp holding the member definitions and the matching explicit instantiation definitions for those two types, and no others.
- Consequence you must preserve: a translation unit that uses campus::Ledger<double> must still COMPILE but must FAIL TO LINK against src/ledger.cpp, while the same translation unit using campus::Ledger<int> links and runs.

PART 3 - implement campus::route in src/campus.cpp. These rules are complete; there are no others.
- A walk starts in room `from` and moves through doors. Traversing a door adds that door's cost() to the walk's total cost and counts as one step.
- On entering a room you pick up the key that room holds, if it holds one. This includes the starting room. Keys are kept for the rest of the walk and are never used up.
- A door whose lock colour is empty can always be traversed. A door with lock colour X can be traversed only while carrying a key of colour X.
- A walk may pass through the same room, and the same door, more than once, with one limit: no room may be ENTERED more than twice in the whole walk. Arriving in the starting room at the very beginning counts as that room's first entry.
- Among all legal walks from `from` to `to`, pick the best one by comparing, in this order: (1) smallest total cost, (2) then fewest steps, (3) then the smallest sequence of room names compared element by element, where the first position at which two sequences differ decides it by ordinary string comparison.
- The result is the room names in walk order joined with '>', for example "atrium>forge". A walk from a room to itself has zero cost and zero steps and returns just that room name.
- Return "none" if either name is not a room of this campus, or if no legal walk exists.
